صِلَآءٌ Roasted, broiled, or fried, flesh-meat. (S, M, K.) ―
-b2- And, as also ↓ صَلًى , (S, M, K,) the former with kesr and the latter with fet-h, (S,) Fuel; (S, * M, K;) syn. وَقُودٌ; (M, K, TA; [in the CK, erroneously, وُقُود;]) i. e. مَا تُوقَدُ بِهِ النَّارُ; (TA;) you say صِلَآءُ النَّارِ and صَلَى النَّارِ: (S:) or both signify fire: (M, Mgh, K:) or صِلَآءٌ signifies the heat of fire. (Msb.) One says, هُوَ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ الصِّلَآءِ فِى الشِّتَآءِ [It, or he, is better than fire in winter]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
